newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROTTERDAM WANTS EARLY FEYENOORD-AJAX KICK-OFF.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ROTTERDAM WANTS EARLY FEYENOORD-AJAX KICK-OFF.

text.p: The mayor of Rotterdam has asked the Dutch soccer association (KNVB) to switch Sunday's evening league fixture between Feyenoord and Ajax Amsterdam to the afternoon.
Bram Peper said that he wanted the 6.00pm (1700 GMT) game brought forward to 14.30pm (1330 GMT) so that police could more easily control supporters.
As mayor, Peper is chief of the Rotterdam police and can introduce special decrees if he thinks public order may be disrupted.
Police expect up to 50,000 rival Feyenoord and Ajax fans to attend the game, one of the classics of the Dutch soccer calendar. The two camps have a history of hooliganism.
The KNVB has not yet responded officially, but the ANP news agency quoted a KNVB spokesman as saying the association would prefer at this stage to stay with the evening kick-off.

"For the time being, the game will kick-off as scheduled. That has nothing to do with planned live television coverage. The (Rotterdam) police agreed to the schedule at the beginning of the season and we plan to stick to that," the spokesman was quoted as saying.

ANP quoted Feyenoord chairman Jorien van den Herik, in Spain to watch the goalless UEFA Cup third round first leg between Tenerife and Feyenoord, as saying that the club would abide by whatever decision was made.
"The mayor is responsible for maintaining public order. If he says it would be better to control fans during daylight, then we can't ignore that."
